transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM), Rachel (Aurora Dir Infra), Sam (Aurora SRE), Marta (Aurora Security)

[00:00] Evan: ok hi everyone thanks for doing the follow-up. can you hear me all right?
[00:07] Rachel: yeah loud and clear, thanks Evan. appreciate you setting this up.
[00:11] Evan: quick agenda - recap timeline, root cause discussion, mitigations we implemented, next steps for the dedicated pilot and security artifacts. sound good?
[00:18] Sam: yep that works. we also want to confirm impact window for our SLAs and what rollback options exist.
[00:22] Priya: great, i'll start with a short timeline that we pulled from infra logs - i know there was some noisy egress at 10:12 UTC and then a cascade of kv cache misses around 10:14 that amplified token generation latency.
[00:32] Priya: (slight stutter) so the model started to thrash on kv cache, TTLs were short-ish for some warmup keys, and then our routing fallback added extra latency as requests moved from cached hosts to cold ones.
[00:42] Sam: can you say "kv cache" again? sometimes the transcript gives us kv-cache as k-v cache, but yes we saw TTL drops...
[00:47] Priya: sorry yeah kv cache eviction - we saw 85% miss rate for a hot prefix for about two minutes. that caused generation to go from avg 180ms/token to ~1.1s/token for affected requests.
[00:58] Rachel: that matches our metrics, we saw error budgets burn between 10:13 and 10:16, roughly three minutes of elevated p95s. customer-facing slowness hit a few dashboards.
[01:07] Marta: security perspective - we flagged a concurrent config push to the VPC firewall rules from the cloud team at 10:11, that coincides with an increase in retransmits. not saying it's the cause but it's correlated.
[01:18] Priya: yep we observed higher packet loss on a specific egress path which increased request latencies to the cache tier; combined with TTL churn it amplified.
[01:25] Evan: ok so root cause working hypothesis = cache eviction hot prefix + transient network degradation (egress path) leading to routing fallbacks and cascading latency; does that feel accurate to everyone?
[01:33] Sam: yes thats fair. i would add that our autoscaler didn't kick fast enough - burst was higher than expected.
[01:38] Priya: on autoscaling, we saw that the thresholds were tuned for steady state, not for the sudden cache miss bursts where cpu/mem spiked on backend hosts. we've recommended lowering the scale threshold and exposing a burst policy.
[01:47] Rachel: on the customer side we want an explanation i can send to ops leadership: is this something that will recur, or is it addressable with config changes?
[01:54] Evan: short answer: short-term config mitigations reduce probability (TTL tweaks, burst autoscale, route hardening), long-term we recommend a dedicated capacity pilot for critical endpoints to remove noisy multi-tenant effects.
[02:05] Sam: about dedicated capacity - how quickly can that be provisioned? and what's the cost tradeoff vs hosted?
[02:11] Evan: we can provision a small dedicated pool within 5 business days for an initial pilot; i'll send pricing delta in the spreadsheet. expected cost up is measurable but we give options for preemptible burst and mixed routing to save dollars.
[02:20] Priest? [sic] Priya: (laugh) i think you meant Priya.
[02:23] Priya: also we have an optimization on kv cache TTLs - for your workload patterns we recommend increasing warm prefix TTL from 30s to 5m for session-start prefixes, this alone should drop miss rate dramatically.
[02:33] Marta: are there any security concerns with longer TTLs? persistent keys, residency?
[02:37] Priya: no, TTL extension is data-handling neutral - doesn't change storage duration beyond cache layer and respects your retention policies. but we'll document it for SOC2 auditors.
[02:45] Marta: good want that in writing. also we need the KMS key rotation logs and confirmation of HSM usage for dedicated if we go that route.
[02:53] Evan: noted - we'll include KMS/HSM config and SOC2 artifacts in the package.
[02:57] Sam: you mentioned kernel-level logs earlier, what specifically will you share?
[03:01] Priya: we'll pull kernel scheduling spikes, socket retransmit counts, and the KV cache heatmap over the incident window - helps show whether evictions were due to memory pressure or eviction policy.
[03:11] Sam: perfect. that will help us correlate with our firewall rule change.
[03:14] Rachel: any immediate mitigations we can enable without downtime?
[03:18] Priya: yes - TTL change for specific prefixes is a config flip no-restart, route hardening to prefer internal egress paths, and an autoscaler tweak (lower threshold, enable burst policy) which is a parameter change. we can push all three as quick wins.
[03:30] Evan: propose we do a staged roll - first TTL and route hardening in the next 24-48 hours, monitor; then autoscaler policy after one small canary.
[03:39] Sam: ok that's reasonable. can we also have a synthetic traffic run to validate?
[03:43] Priya: yes we can run a replay of the traffic window with a KV cache warmup step; we recommend running it in a staging project or during low-traffic window.
[03:51] Marta: security request: redwood to provide evidence of encryption in transit for cache traffic, and a network diagram showing egress paths for dedicated.
[03:59] Evan: we'll attach the network diagram and TLS config doc.
[04:02] Liam: quick note - i've created a shared folder with the postmortem draft, logs and the bench spreadsheet link: https://files.redwood.example/aurora/pm-20260310 (link shared in chat).
[04:12] Rachel: got it, saw the link. looks like priya already uploaded initial heatmaps.
[04:16] Priya: yes that was preliminary; i'll refine and add kernel-level traces.
[04:20] Sam: when we do the dedicated pilot, can we pin model versions? we saw a small regression when a new model variant got auto-deployed.
[04:27] Evan: absolutely - dedicated allows pinning and controlled rollouts, canary and A/B as well. we'll propose a pinned rollout for pilot.
[04:33] Rachel: any concerns about quality regressions with quantization changes you may recommend for cost?
[04:38] Priya: we'll avoid aggressive quantization during pilot; recommendations will include mild quantization and quality monitoring tied to a prompt set you provide.
[04:45] Sam: who will own rollbacks if the pilot triggers issues?
[04:49] Evan: operationally Redwood can do immediate model revert and route traffic back to hosted endpoints, or we can implement an automatic fallback policy. we'll document the rollback playbook.
[04:58] Marta: SOC2: we'll need a window of what data touched cache, retention durations, and proof of audit logging for access to KMS keys.
[05:06] Priya: we'll export audit logs and a KMS access timeline. note some logs are retained in the private control plane when you're on Dedicated; we'll clarify differences in the artifact package.
[05:17] Evan: ok let's move to timelines and owners - (summarizes) priya to deliver logs & heatmaps by 2026-03-18, evan to send pilot proposal & pricing by 2026-03-19, sam to give traffic window and repro steps by 2026-03-18, marta to provide SOC2 scoping questions by 2026-03-20, liam to set weekly pilot cadence starting 2026-03-24.
[05:35] Rachel: noted. one question on cost: if we do dedicated for just critical endpoints, does Redwood support mixed routing?
[05:41] Evan: yes mixed routing is supported - you can route critical paths to dedicated pool and keep non-critical on hosted. that keeps cost targeted.
[05:47] Sam: any quick wins on autoscaler tuning you can share now?
[05:50] Priya: lower scale-in/scale-out thresholds, add a short-term overprovision buffer (1.2x) for known spike windows, and enable a faster scale-up cooldown. i'll send concrete numbers in the plan.
[05:59] Rachel: ok sounds good. is there an SLA credit conversation here? we had customer-facing impact, can we expect a credit?
[06:05] Liam: we'll need to correlate the impact window with your contracted SLA terms; i'll open a ticket with billing and loop you in - expect an initial reply within 48 hours.
[06:12] Marta: last security note - if we go dedicated we need a defined KMS workflow for key rotation and access policies. also please confirm HSM-backed keys are available in our region.
[06:20] Priya: HSM-backed keys are available - we'll detail region support and rotation patterns in the docs we send.
[06:25] Evan: ok any other open items?
[06:28] Rachel: none from infra. thanks everyone.
[06:31] Sam: thanks.
[06:33] Evan: we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the pilot planning meeting - thanks all.
